messages:
Maya (Support): Customer ACME reporting intermittent 400s from /v1/embeddings and big tail latency spikes when using batching on their dedicated pool. Attaching sample payload and a short repro log.

ACME-SRE: sample request they used:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "model": "embed-64-v2", "input": ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"] }
```
Observed error: `400 Bad Request: embedding dimension mismatch` — but weirdly single-item requests succeed. Tail latency during peak is ~2.5–5s for some batches.

Jordan (Eng-Oncall): sounds like mixed dimensions getting coalesced into a single batch. What are their batching settings and do they have multiple model variants behind the same route?

Maya (Support): customer reported route config (from their console):
```
max_batch_size: 256
dynamic_batching: true
batch_window_ms: 20
```
They also rolled a new smaller-dim model last week and left the alias unchanged.

Priya (ML Infra): that batch_window_ms is pretty tight. With dynamic batching enabled the runtime will try to coalesce across inflight requests; if different model variants with incompatible embedding dims are coalesced, the batch validator drops the batch -> `400`. Also, aggressive batching + high max_batch_size can amplify tail latency because the pipeline waits for either size or timeout.

ACME-SRE: confirmed: we have two variants behind the alias: `embed-128-v1` (legacy) and `embed-64-v2` (new). Some clients still call the old variant. Repro script attached: they hit the alias and sometimes the requests get routed to different backends, leading to mixed-dimension batches.

Jordan (Eng-Oncall): short-term mitigations: 1) pin model version on requests via header `x-model-version: embed-64-v2`; 2) reduce `max_batch_size` to 1 or a very small number to avoid coalescing; 3) disable dynamic batching on that route. Any of those will stop the 400s but have throughput/cost tradeoffs.

Maya (Support): customer tried `x-model-version` header — 400s disappeared but throughput dropped ~3x (expected). They asked if we can avoid such a hard tradeoff.

Priya (ML Infra): medium-term: add a route-level setting to require `batch_variant_consistency: strict` so runtime never mixes model variants. That lets batching stay enabled but only coalesces identical-dim variants. Also proposing clearer server-side validation: return `422 Unprocessable Entity` with model ids and offending dims instead of generic 400 so customers can triage faster. Filing follow-up.

Jordan (Eng-Oncall): logged ENG-1129 to add clearer error + metric (embed.dim_conflicts) and ENG-1130 for route-level `batch_variant_consistency`. For immediate customer guidance: recommend `max_batch_size: 32` and bump `batch_window_ms` to 50–100ms to reduce tail while preserving batching. Example snippet: 
```
route:
  max_batch_size: 32
  dynamic_batching: true
  batch_window_ms: 50
  batch_variant_consistency: strict
```
That should reduce long tails and avoid cross-variant coalescing.

ACME-SRE: applied the config suggestion (reduced max batch, increased window, strict variant). Results: 99.9th percentile tail went from ~4.8s -> ~1.1s, 400 errors stopped. Still testing throughput; looks acceptable.

Maya (Support): great — customer reports improved latency and no more dimension errors. Leaving open for one more day for SLA confirmation. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy #12345 to inference-runtime succeeded :shipit:

Maya (Support): follow-ups: Jordan to update ENG tickets with rollout plan; Priya to propose server-side error improvements. I'll close after ACME confirms tomorrow.
